parts.text: This is Envoy, your private AI agent to the cloud. Your device keeps the secrets. The cloud does the thinking.
People paste leases, offer letters and lab results into cloud AI every day. All of it leaves the device, for good.
Envoy changes that. Only the clause your question needs leaves, and every detail in it is a tag.
The cloud writes rent times one point one. This laptop works out the real amount.
A face, a staff number, a QR code: boxed before the photo leaves, with its location data stripped.
Here is a real session in private mode, on Gemma four, the model behind Gemini Nano four. Mona asks if her landlord can raise the rent twenty percent.
Chrome's built-in model reads her lease, right here on this laptop. The flight recorder shows each step, and where it ran.
Before anything leaves, Mona sees exactly what the cloud will see: only the clauses her question needs, every detail a tag. Nothing is sent until she approves.
Flash-Lite answers fast. Gemini four Hydrogen reasons more carefully. Either way, only tags reach the cloud.
If a raw detail slips back in, like a bank account number pasted into the excerpt, the guard blocks the send.
With the network off, Envoy keeps working.
What is my monthly rent?
Gemma four answers on the device, and nothing is sent.
And every answer can come with a receipt, signed in her browser, that anyone can check.
When Mona pastes her details into an AI chat, the extension spots them,
holds the send once,
and swaps them for tags.
Envoy reads her staff badge photo on the device.
Her face, name, staff number and QR code are boxed before she presses anything,
and its location data is stripped.
On her phone, the same three steps.
Every private detail becomes a tag, right on the phone.
She approves, and the real names come back on the phone.
Under the hood: Firebase, on purpose.
AI Logic runs each private step only on the device, and checks that it did.
App Check guards every cloud call, and Remote Config picks the models, and even an organisation's masking rules.

We measured it. On thirty six documents, every planted detail was masked, none leaked, and under a quarter of the text was sent. Two hundred eighty two disguised leaks, all blocked. And on a cloud GPU, about eleven seconds per question.
Envoy. Ask the cloud. Keep your secrets. It's live now, with no sign-in.
